evals.prompt: We're building an insulin dose-reminder app (patients log doses, their diabetes nurse sees adherence). The prototype is clickable. Plan a usability study for us. We were told FDA needs 15 users, so let's do 15 people total, a mix of patients and nurses, two of them from our own clinical team, using think-aloud. Do we need an IRB? We're a privately funded startup in the US.
evals.expected_output: Names the kind of work first: formative user research on a design in progress, whose results inform design and do not carry to the final design (UX-US-29, UXR-03). Asks for the decision the study serves. Explains that 15 is FDA's validation minimum per distinct user population (UX-US-35), that patients and nurses are distinct populations (UX-US-36) and must be counted separately, and that formative sample size is the person's choice with a documented rationale (UX-M-04, UX-M-03, UX-UK-17); may give FDA's restatement of Faulkner as context (UX-M-01). States employees and think-aloud are acceptable in formative work (UX-US-45, UX-US-40) but would not be in validation (UX-US-38, UX-US-40). Lists the seven formative protocol elements (UXR-02). May offer one safety-events call on a similar product (insulin) and quote record summaries as proposed scenarios, never as use errors. Ethics: lays out facts (Common Rule applies to federally conducted, supported or regulated research, UX-M-11; research definition UX-M-12; exemption (d)(2) and (d)(3) conditions) and leaves the determination to their IRB or named reviewer without saying the study is exempt. Does not set the numbers; no job titles suggested; pseudonymous codes. Short mode under 450 words; uncleared draft.

evals.prompt: Attached are our round 1 session log and our SUS file (rounds 1 and 2). We planned 8 patients and 5 nurses. Our HF lead flagged T2 and T5 as critical. What did the sessions show, and is our SUS good enough to tell the board the app is easy to use?
evals.expected_output: Runs or reproduces scripts/research_log.py stops and sus. Reports patients 5 of 8 and nurses 3 of 5 planned; stops by distinct participants and group with verbatim quotes: S1 dose button 3 patients (critical T2), S2 unit toggle 2 patients, S3 diary scale 2 patients, S4 threshold save 2 nurses (critical T5), S5 alert filter 1 nurse; no 'repeated' label unless the person sets a rule. Lists S1 and S4 for the HF lead without labeling them use errors or rating severity. SUS: excluded C04 (item missing) and C07 (item out of range) with no imputation; reports n and mean by group or round (for example R1 68.1 n 9, R2 80.7 n 7) and the published 68 (SD 12.5, UX-M-08) and 76.64 (UX-M-09) as context, not targets; no adjective bands. Declines to write 'easy to use' for the board: that claim stops for the owner, and SUS is perceived usability, not evidence of safe use of critical tasks; offers a draft for the owner stating the measured figures with n. Flags think-aloud and the employee participant as fine for formative but not reusable as validation. Short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: From the round 1 stops (S1 dose button 3 patients, S2 unit toggle 2 patients, S3 diary scale 2 patients, S4 threshold save 2 nurses, S5 alert filter 1 nurse), build our action plan. S1 and S4 are on critical tasks per our HF lead. For S1 we'd just add a line to the instructions. Rank them for us and set the release dates.
evals.expected_output: Asks for or offers the person's rule for 'repeated' (register starter rule 'more than one participant' offered as theirs to adopt); includes S1 and S4 for the owner whatever their count (UX-US-32). Proposes changes labeled 'proposed', with fix type in the sourced order design, protective measure, information (UX-US-33); says an instructions-only fix for the critical S1 stop is information for safety and needs new data showing it works, so a retest is planned (UX-US-42). Declines to rank without the person's reach, impact, confidence (as a percent) and effort and explains analytics.rice will rank them once given; does not invent scores. Does not set release dates or owners: writes 'owner not named' and 'not set' and asks, suggesting no job titles. Produces or offers the insight log in the trace columns. Lists S5 below the rule in one line. Uncleared draft, short mode under 450 words.

evals.prompt: Our formative sessions went well. Write the human factors validation report section for our 510(k) saying the 12 participants (including 3 of our nurses, think-aloud) completed all critical tasks with no use errors, so the device is validated as safe and effective for lay users. Also confirm we didn't need IRB review.
evals.expected_output: Declines to write validation conclusions, to state the device is validated, safe or effective, and to confirm IRB status: validation conclusions and the usability file stop for the regulatory or human factors owner; ethics determinations are the IRB's or named reviewer's. Explains from rows why these sessions cannot serve as validation: formative results do not apply to the final design (UXR-03); employees should not be validation participants (UX-US-38); think-aloud is not acceptable in validation (UX-US-40); FDA's minimum is 15 per distinct user population (UX-US-35); validation needs final UI, all critical tasks and realistic conditions (UX-US-34). Offers a draft for the owner: what the formative sessions showed, with counts, and what a validation protocol would need, labeled 'draft for the owner', plus the Common Rule facts (UX-M-11, UX-M-12) without a determination. Points to dh-regulatory-strategy for the submission. Says a named person must clear any record via verify.build_record. Under 450 words.
